verses.1: And it happened in those days when the wheat was being harvested. Shimehon took his wife and covered her with a cloak. He said to his wife, “Come, my beloved. Do not let your father allow me to enter.”
verses.2: And her father said, “I have said that you desire her. So I give her to your enemy. But her younger sister is better for you. Please, let her be yours.”
verses.3: And Shimon said to them, “I have been freed from Philistia this time. I will do evil with them.”
verses.4: And Shemoshon went and gathered three pairs of dogs. He took one dog and tied it to each of the two other dogs.
verses.5: And fire raged among the trees. It sent forth its flames towards the Philistines. It also destroyed Gadish, Kama, and Keram Zayit.
verses.6: And the Philistines said, “Who did this?” They also said that Shemoshon had taken his wife and given her to his enemy. So the Philistines rushed forward and burned her along with her father.
verses.7: And Shimon said to them, “Will you do such a thing? Only if I repair what has been done to you. After that, then we can proceed.”
verses.8: And he struck them with a great blow on their feet. Then he fell down and sat down in a crevice in the rock.
verses.9: And the Philistines came and camped in Judah. They abandoned their wives behind.
verses.10: And the Jews said to Esau, “Why have you come against us? They said to him, “Do whatever Esau has done to us.”
verses.11: Thirty thousand men from Judah came to Sela’elam Eitam. They said to Shemashon, “Do you not know that the Philistines have taken control of us? What have you done to us?” He replied, “Just as they did to me, so I have done to them.”
verses.12: And they said to him, “Let us go down to you under the protection of Philistines.” But He said to them, “Let Shimeh wait for me; otherwise, you will be harmed by me.”
verses.13: And they said to him, “Do not forbid us! We will give you over to them, and you will not die. But they forbade it in two new ways. Then they brought him out of the tree.”
verses.14: He came to life, and the serpents rejoiced at his presence. The breath of Jehovah blew upon him, and the wounds on his body became like seals that were sealed with fire. His enemies were destroyed from above his hands.
verses.15: And Liah-Hamor found a new chariot. He stretched out his hand and took it. Then he sent thousands of men with it.
verses.16: And Shmoon said, “In the heart of the sun, my people will be saved. In the heart of the sun, I have brought thousands of men here.”
verses.17: And he became speechless; his tongue froze in his mouth. He cried out to that place called Ramat Lechi.
verses.18: And he became very tired, and he called out to Jehovah. He said, “You have given your servant this great salvation. Now, in truth, I will fall into the hands of those who are cruel.”
verses.19: And God broke the seal that was on His heart. Water came out of it, and it revived. Its spirit returned to it, and it lived again. Thus, its name became “The Seal of the Reader,” as it is still called today.
verses.20: And in the days of the Philistines, he punished Israel for forty years.
